questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.**

Which movie __have you watched__ on television when I called you?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'were you watching'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The underlined part in the given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here, **'were you watching'** should be used instead of **'have you watched'.**
 
• The former part of the given sentence must be in **the past continuous tense **so the verb must be used in its** past continuous form(was/were + V-ing)** and not in the **present** **perfect form(have + V₃). **
 
• The **'past continuous'** describes actions or events in a time before now, which began in the **past** and were still going on when another event occurred.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 3.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *Which movie **were you watching** on television when I called you?*

questions.question:
**Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. Firstly, it provides air for respiration, serves the sense of smell and conditions the air by filtering, warming and moistening it.

B. The nose is the prominent structure between the eyes that serves as the entrance to the respiratory tract.

C. For inhalation it has two cavities, separated from one another by a wall of cartilage called the septum.

D. Apart from filtering the air, it also cleans itself of foreign debris extracted from inhalations.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**BADC**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given question is an example of a Para Jumble.
 
• We know that the first statement of a para jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, starting of an incident, or it begins with 'most' or 'once'.
 
 
• **Sentence B** will be the starting line as it contains the main idea of the para jumble i.e. nose is the prominent structure of the respiratory tract.
 
• However, **Sentence A** states that it provides air for respiration, serves the sense of smell, and conditions the air by filtering, warming, and moistening it.
 
• So, **A** will follow **B**.
 
• Further, **Sentence D** states that apart from filtering the air, it also cleans itself of foreign debris extracted from Inhalations and sentence C says that for inhalation it has two cavities.
 
• So, **C** will follow **D**. 
 
• Thus, the correct sequence is:
 
 
• **B**: The nose is the prominent structure between the eyes that serves as the entrance to the respiratory tract.
 
• **A**: Firstly, it provides air for respiration, serves the sense of smell and conditions the air by filtering, warming and moistening it.
 
• **D**: Apart from filtering the air, it also cleans itself of foreign debris extracted from inhalations.
 
• **C**: For inhalation it has two cavities, separated from one another by a wall of cartilage called the septum.

 
 
 
 
 

**Correct Sequence:__** *The nose is the prominent structure between the eyes that serves as the entrance to the respiratory tract. Firstly, it provides air for respiration, serves the sense of smell and conditions the air by filtering, warming and moistening it. Apart from filtering the air, it also cleans itself of foreign debris extracted from inhalations. For inhalation it has two cavities, separated from one another by a wall of cartilage called the septum.*

It has / been raining / since / two hours.
questions.solution:

__
 
• The given sentence is** grammatically incorrect.**
 
• Here, '**for**' should be used instead of '**since**'.
 
• ‘**For**’ refers to a specific period of time or a numerical value of time, for example for*** 2 years, for 4 weeks, for 3 hours, etc.***
 
• However, in the given question, the period of time is **2 hours. **
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 3.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *It has been raining **for** two hours.*

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.**

Every Saturday, / the workers gets / their weekly wages.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is** 'the workers gets'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here,** 'the workers get' **should be used instead of** 'the workers gets'.**
 
• According to the **“Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”**,** a singular subject **always takes** a singular verb **and **a plural subject** always takes **a plural verb.**
 
• In the given sentence, ‘**workers**’ is a plural subject that will take ‘**get**’ as **a plural verb. **
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *Every Saturday, **the workers get **their weekly wages.*

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

The judge found the prisoner guilty.

options.text: The prisoner has been found guilty by the judge
The prisoner had been found guilty by the judge.
The prisoner was found guilty by the judge.
The judge was found guilty by the prisoner.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'The prisoner was found guilty by the judge'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in Active Voice. As per the given question, we have to change it into Passive Voice. 
 
• The structure of the given sentence is as follows:
 
 
• Subject + V2+ Object. (Active Voice)
 
• Subject (objective case)+ was/were + V3 + Object (subjective case). (Passive Voice)
 
 
 
• *Example:*
 
 
• *Their cousin showed them some rare photographs. (Active Voice)*
 
• *They were shown some rare photographs by their cousin. (Passive Voice)*
 
 
 
• The subject of the given sentence is 'The judge'.​​
 
• The object of the given sentence is 'the prisoner'. 
 
• The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject.
 
• And 'found' will be changed into 'was found'. 

 ​

Correct Sentence:__ *The prisoner was found guilty by the judge.*
